title: Software Engineering
tagline: Software processes, requirements, architecture, design principles, version control, testing, refactoring, verification and professional ethics
summary: Software engineering is programming done by teams, over years, for people who depend on the result. This course covers how real software is specified, designed, built, tested and maintained: development processes and requirements, architecture and design principles, version control and continuous integration, testing, refactoring and maintenance, verification of critical software, and the professional and ethical responsibilities of engineers.

chapters.title: Software processes
chapters.summary: Life-cycle models, plan-driven and agile development, and estimating and managing software projects.

chapters.title: Requirements
chapters.summary: Eliciting, specifying and validating requirements, with user stories and use cases.

chapters.title: Software architecture
chapters.summary: Architectural styles such as layered, client–server and event-driven systems, and recording design decisions.

chapters.title: Design principles
chapters.summary: Coupling and cohesion, information hiding, the SOLID principles and designing for change.

chapters.title: Version control and collaboration
chapters.summary: Git, branching and merging, code review and continuous integration.

chapters.title: Software testing
chapters.summary: Unit, integration and system tests, test design and coverage, and test-driven development.

chapters.title: Refactoring and maintenance
chapters.summary: Code smells, refactoring, technical debt and working with legacy code.

chapters.title: Reliability and verification
chapters.summary: Static analysis, formal specification, model checking and safety-critical software.

chapters.title: Professional practice and ethics
chapters.summary: Licences and intellectual property, privacy, accessibility, accountability and codes of ethics.
